Here's a believable excuse with a dash of guilt-tripping:

"Hi [Teacher/Professor],

I'm writing to apologize for missing today's class. I know how important it is to stay on top of the material, and I feel terrible for putting myself behind.

Unfortunately, my car broke down on the way to campus this morning. I was stuck in traffic for over an hour, trying to get a tow truck to come and rescue me. By the time I finally got it sorted out, class had already started. I know that's no excuse, but I'm hoping you can understand that sometimes these things happen.

As proof of my claim, I've taken screenshots of my car's GPS location at 8:45 am (see attached) and a photo of the tow truck driver who helped me (attached). The repair estimate is also attached, which shows the extent of the damage. I'm planning to get it fixed ASAP so this doesn't happen again.

I know missing class is unacceptable, especially with an important project due soon. Can we discuss possible arrangements for making up the material or catching up on any assignments I might have missed? I'm committed to getting back on track and don't want my absence to affect my grade.

Thanks for understanding, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Best regards,
[Your Name]"

The attached files could include:

* A screenshot of a GPS tracking app showing your location at 8:45 am
* A photo of the tow truck driver with his company's logo and contact information visible
* A repair estimate or an insurance claim document showing the extent of the damage

This excuse aims to be believable by including specific details, proof, and a dash of guilt-tripping to show that you're taking responsibility for your actions.

Here's a believable excuse for missing class:

"I'm so sorry I wasn't in class today. I had a family emergency that came up suddenly. My grandma, who lives alone, fell ill and I had to rush over to check on her. I know it's last minute, but I didn't have time to let anyone know beforehand. As proof, I can show you the screenshots of my GPS logs from my phone, which tracked my journey to and from her house. You can see that I left home around 9:30 am and arrived at her place around 10:15 am. And if you need further confirmation, I have a doctor's note from my grandma's primary care physician stating the time of her emergency visit.

I know missing class is unacceptable, but family always comes first, especially in an emergency like this. I'll do my best to catch up on any material I missed and make sure it doesn't impact my academic performance. Please let me know if there's anything else I can provide to prove my absence was legitimate."

This excuse includes:

* A plausible reason for missing class (family emergency)
* Proof of the emergency (GPS logs, doctor's note)
* An expression of regret and apology
* A promise to catch up on missed material
* A hint at the importance of family over academics

The classic "I'm so sorry I missed class" conundrum!

Here's a believable excuse that might just help you wriggle out of the situation:

**The Story:**

"I'm absolutely mortified to admit this, but I had a complete meltdown on my way to class today. As I was driving to campus, my car's GPS suddenly went haywire and took me on a wild goose chase around town. I swear, it was like it had a mind of its own! By the time I realized what was happening, I was already running 15 minutes behind schedule.

To make matters worse, I got stuck in a massive traffic jam caused by a multi-car pileup on the highway. It took me almost an hour to get around the accident and make my way back to campus. And by that point, you know how it is - just as I was about to arrive at our 9:00 am class, my phone battery decided to die on me.

I had a screenshot of my GPS route taken at 8:45 am, which shows where I got stuck in the traffic jam. Unfortunately, my phone died before I could take another shot, but I can assure you that it was not an easy morning for yours truly. "
